name: Starlink VisorSat
note: Benchmarking M4 reference model for Mallama (2021). V1.x chassis in 'shark-fin' operational mode with the deployable visor. Body frame: +Z nadir, +X toward the Sun's azimuth (the bus yaws so the visor stays sunward), +Y = +Z x +X. Every number is covered by `sources`; the visor's scale, bus_metal, antenna_white and visor_black are calibrated to MMT tracks (see their sources).

sources.value: bus 1.3 x 2.8 m footprint, 0.2 m thick
sources.source: Footprint: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5 row: bus 2.8 x 1.3 m; V1.0 'about 3 m bus', same chassis family). Thickness: 60-satellite stack of 6.7 m in the Falcon 9 fairing (lilibots.blogspot.com, 2020-04, secondary estimate).

sources.subject: antennas
sources.value: white antenna region 0.9 x 2.2 m centred on the nadir face (63% of the base); range 40-80%
sources.source: Cole 2021 (arXiv:2107.06026) section 2: 'white antenna panels on the base', base otherwise polished metal. Region size not published.

sources.subject: visor
sources.value: black sheet 1.29 x 2.2 m under the antenna region, reaching 0.39 m sunward of the antennas' edge (0.19 m past the bus side), 0.166 m below the base
sources.source: Radio-transparent foam that blocks sunlight from the antennas (SpaceX via Tesmanian 2020, SpaceNews 2020). Cole 2021 section 3.2: antennas fully shaded at 23 deg Sun depression, light leaks under at smaller angles - so gap = inset x tan 23 deg (derived). The scale is unpublished and was FITTED: inset 0.39 m (gap 0.166 m), starlink_refit 2026-10-22: joint fit, both designs, to 42 Mini-MegaTORTORA tracks (STARLINK-1008 2020/22/24, STARLINK-1436; 1.5-s medians of MMT's magnitude above the atmosphere vs SatModelTool --pass), held out STARLINK-1538 (29 tracks) and STARLINK-1008 2021/23/25 (10); 13 VisorSat bright-attitude tracks excluded (unmodelled attitude). Until then 0.55 m (M8, 2026-09-23), fitted to the mallama2021_visorsat phase curve under SatBench's then-assumed Sun -18..-6 deg window.

sources.subject: solar_array
sources.value: one 2.8 x 8.1 m array, cells facing the Sun's azimuth
sources.source: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5: solar array 2.8 x 8.1 m). Hinge at the centre of the bus top: estimate.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: base to nadir, visor side yawed to the Sun's azimuth
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2 ('base and its antennas face the Earth') and section 5 ('the visor must remain pointing to the Sun-azimuth for it to work'); SpaceX 'shark-fin' operational mode (Tesmanian 2020).

sources.subject: array
sources.value: fixed 24 deg from local vertical, top leaning away from the Sun (95% range 14-34 deg)
sources.source: Cole 2021 Table 3 (late-2020 fit, the Mallama 2021 period): panel offset angle 24 deg away from Sun azimuth, fixed to the local vertical rather than Sun-tracking (section 4.2 item 3). June 2021 data fit -5 deg instead (section 6).

sources.subject: bus_metal
sources.value: aluminium, F0 0.9 (preset), Beckmann alpha 0.08, diffuse albedo 0.11, Minnaert k 0.65
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: base is 'polished metal'. F0 0.9 = bare aluminium's normal-incidence reflectance at 550 nm (kept, not fitted). Lobe shape, diffuse floor and the Minnaert exponent are calibrated: starlink_refit 2026-10-22: joint fit, both designs, to 42 Mini-MegaTORTORA tracks (STARLINK-1008 2020/22/24, STARLINK-1436; 1.5-s medians of MMT's magnitude above the atmosphere vs SatModelTool --pass), held out STARLINK-1538 (29 tracks) and STARLINK-1008 2021/23/25 (10); 13 VisorSat bright-attitude tracks excluded (unmodelled attitude). With the GGX tail of the earlier alpha 0.23 (M8, fitted under SatBench's then-assumed Sun -18..-6 deg window, which MMT's -24..-11 does not match) every free fit drove F0 to its floor: MMT sees the base's off-specular tail at phase 75-110 deg ~2x fainter than GGX predicts. A sharp Beckmann lobe (alpha 0.08) reaches that loss with F0 0.9 (Beckmann 0.15: loss +23%). Cole Table 3's exponents 24/52 belong to a BRDF without Fresnel or masking and are not used. Diffuse 0.11: residual contamination / seams. Minnaert k 0.65 on the nadir face's diffuse terms (bus_metal, antenna_white, visor_black): Mallama 2020a's own flat-panel regression on 830 V1.0 passes gives 0.578 +- 0.084; the MMT residual's Sun-altitude trend (Lambert: -0.29 / -0.36 mag per 10 deg, V1.0 / VisorSat fit tracks) is flat at k ~0.55 for V1.0, and the free fit lands at 0.80 (loss 0.1412 vs 0.1426 at 0.65, 0.1439 Lambert): 0.65 is inside Mallama's 1 sigma and takes the trend to -0.07 / -0.22.

sources.subject: antenna_white
sources.value: white paint preset, diffuse albedo 0.31, Minnaert k 0.65
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: 'white antenna panels'. Albedo FITTED (the preset's 0.8 was an estimate): starlink_refit 2026-10-22: joint fit, both designs, to 42 Mini-MegaTORTORA tracks (STARLINK-1008 2020/22/24, STARLINK-1436; 1.5-s medians of MMT's magnitude above the atmosphere vs SatModelTool --pass), held out STARLINK-1538 (29 tracks) and STARLINK-1008 2021/23/25 (10); 13 VisorSat bright-attitude tracks excluded (unmodelled attitude). 0.31 x the 0.9 x 2.2 m region is degenerate with a smaller region at a higher albedo; the region size is unpublished, so the albedo carries it. Minnaert k 0.65 on the nadir face's diffuse terms (bus_metal, antenna_white, visor_black): Mallama 2020a's own flat-panel regression on 830 V1.0 passes gives 0.578 +- 0.084; the MMT residual's Sun-altitude trend (Lambert: -0.29 / -0.36 mag per 10 deg, V1.0 / VisorSat fit tracks) is flat at k ~0.55 for V1.0, and the free fit lands at 0.80 (loss 0.1412 vs 0.1426 at 0.65, 0.1439 Lambert): 0.65 is inside Mallama's 1 sigma and takes the trend to -0.07 / -0.22.

sources.value: black paint preset (diffuse albedo 0.05); visor_black's albedo 0.019 and Minnaert k 0.65 are calibrated (the visor source)
sources.source: Cole 2021 Figure 2 (black edges added on visorsats) and section 3.2 ('the visor is declared as being black').

sources.subject: array_back_dark
sources.source: Cole 2021 Table 3: rear-face emission b = 0, section 4.2: rear face < 20% of the base.
